title: Information-Geometric Dimensional Collapse in a Finite-Temperature Superintegrable \( \mathfrak{su}(2) \) Fermion Model
content: We investigate the finite-temperature statistical geometry of a quantum superintegrable system consisting of N fermions distributed across two degenerate single-particle levels and governed by a collective quasi-spin su(2) pairing Hamiltonian ˆH (V) = ˆJz − V ˆX. Owing to the model’s commuting algebraic structure and non-Abelian dual symmetry, the energy spectrum is obtained purely algebraically in the Dicke basis | J,M⟩, with each multiplet carrying a large M-independent multiplicity YJ . Because [ ˆH(V), ˆH(V′)] = 0 across the entire coupling space, the canonical thermal states ˆρ(β,V) form a mutually commuting family whose quantum Fisher information metric reduces identically to the classical Fisher–Rao metric on the (β,V) parameter manifold. Expressing the metric determinant det G in terms of the covariance determinant of ˆH and ˆX, we show that hidden symmetries impose a severe low-temperature geometric bottleneck: across almost the entire (β,V) plane, det G → 0 and the effective thermodynamic parameter space collapses from two dimensions down to one or zero. We show that this rare geometric flattening arises from three algebraic mechanisms protected by superintegrability (exact identities, closed-form solutions, or selection rules survive perturbations or deformations because an underlying hidden symmetry algebra forces them to hold) : (i) exponential locking into V-independent ground-state multiplets, (ii) rank-1 collinearity of thermal fluctuations along discrete ground-state level crossings, and (iii) the complete absence of eigenstate hybridization or level repulsion. Local statistical distinguishability is consequently restricted to a finite-temperature crossover dome where at least three non-collinear (J,M) sectors compete.
